One of the things I dislike about Archive is that everything is in PDF format, unformated text, or badly converted epub. When the epub version is compiled, it's either from the text version or a version of the PDF with some formatting. The text file relies on OCR for text detection, which is often unreliable in older books, resulting in an epub that's riddled with typos.

The owner of this site spends a lot of time formatting and cleaning up the text of these old books to make them readable. They're often very attractive and make reading enjoyable. If you find this has value to you, I encourage you to send her some money for her work.
Thanks. I highly value sites like this.

These books are reformatted for ebooks. What's wrong with that, you ask? In the reformatting, information is lost. Often the title page or copyright page is left out entirely. The page numbers do not correspond to the page numbers in the paper version of the work, and if you change the font size, the pagination changes. For this reason, you cannot cite a quotation from an ebook. Worst of all, the people who format ebooks can change or cut out parts of the original text, and you have no way of knowing this was done unless you compare the ebook with the paper version.

A much better policy is to download PDF versions of books that contain the actual scanned page images of the paper books. This way, you know you are getting the exact same book that was sold in book stores.

I can't disagree with what you say. My only issue with PDF is that it's a fixed width format and it's sometimes difficult to read on a handheld tablet or e-reader without the type being too small. Sometimes you can't even trust print books, although it's rare. I'm reading "Revelations" by Jacques Vallee as an epub converted from PDF. I copied the text and images and reformatted it myself using Calibre. I noticed there is a large gap in the text between two images. At the end of one page there is an unfinished sentence, then the next two pages have images, and when the text picks up on the third, it's not the end of previous sentence but is completely unrelated, as if something got left out. This is pretty rare, though.

The other things you mention, such a lack of hyperlinked citations and a table of contents, are completely correct and can be frustrating, especially when you see a number in the text that you know should be a footnote but isn't linked.
